sections.heading: What is AOV?: Average Order Value
paragraphs: AOV, or Average Order Value, is a key eCommerce metric that measures the average amount spent per transaction on your website or store.
Instead of chasing new customers, many businesses focus on increasing AOV to maximize revenue from existing traffic. According to Shopify, the global AOV is approximately $145 across all industries.

bullets.text: Increases Revenue Without More Traffic: Higher AOV means more revenue per customer without additional acquisition costs

bullets.label: Improves Profit Margins
bullets.text: Shipping a $100 order costs the same as shipping a $140 order; the second is more profitable

bullets.label: Offsets Rising Ad Costs
bullets.text: With CPCs rising 15%+ on Meta and Google, higher AOV helps maintain ROAS

bullets.label: Reveals Customer Behavior
bullets.text: Low AOV may indicate pricing issues or missed upselling opportunities

sections.heading: How to Calculate AOV: The Formula
paragraphs: For example, if your store generated $100 in revenue from 100 orders , your AOV is $100 ÷ 100 = $100
This means on average, each customer spends $100 per order .
sections.formula: AOV = Total Revenue ÷ Number of Orders

bullets.label: Free Shipping Thresholds
bullets.text: Set 30% above your current AOV (e.g., "$50 for free shipping")

bullets.label: Product Bundles
bullets.text: Offer "complete the look" or "starter kit" packages at a discount

bullets.label: Loyalty Programs
bullets.text: Reward higher spending with points or exclusive perks

bullets.label: AI Recommendations
bullets.text: Personalized suggestions can increase AOV by 30%+

sections.heading: Pro Tip: Look Beyond the Mean
paragraphs: Marketing experts recommend analyzing not just the mean (average), but also the mode (most common order value). A few high-value orders can skew your average, hiding that most customers spend much less. Focus on improving the modal order value for sustainable gains.
